# Root, link and end paths

`multi.lin.sce` is a simulated trajectory with three end points, made with
dyntoy for the benchmarks of tradeSeq [@saelens2019; @vandenberge2020] and
analysed with Monocle3 [@cao2019]. Its cells carry a hard path label
(`group`) and the Monocle3 pseudotime (`Monocle3_Pseudotime`); the
[Trajectory input](
    https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/trajectory-input.html)
vignette shows how to build such labels.

```{r load-data, message = FALSE}
library(scMaSigPro)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(ggplot2)

data("multi.lin.sce", package = "scMaSigPro")
table(colData(multi.lin.sce)$group)
```

```{r plot-tsne, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   t-SNE of multi.lin.sce, coloured by path label (left) and by Monocle3
#|   pseudotime (right).
tsne <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(multi.lin.sce, "TSNE"))
colnames(tsne) <- c("tSNE1", "tSNE2")
tsne$path <- colData(multi.lin.sce)$group
tsne$pseudotime <- colData(multi.lin.sce)$Monocle3_Pseudotime
p_path <- ggplot(tsne, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, colour = path)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.5) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
p_time <- ggplot(tsne, aes(tSNE1, tSNE2, colour = pseudotime)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.5) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c() +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
patchwork::wrap_plots(p_path, p_time, ncol = 2)
```

The cells start in the `root`, which all three lineages share. One lineage
leads straight to the end path `path_Y_52`; the other two first share a
segment, the link `path_Y_18|path_Y_15`, and then part into the end paths
`path_Y_15` and `path_Y_18`. The pseudotime runs from the root through each
lineage; every lineage shares it.

# The object

The labels are shortened first: the `path_` prefix is dropped and the link
gets the separator `_links_`, the default of `sc.restruct()`. To keep the
vignette fast, the analysis uses the first 200 of the 501 genes.

```{r create-object}
cell_data <- as.data.frame(colData(multi.lin.sce))
cell_data$group <- gsub("path_", "", cell_data$group, fixed = TRUE)
cell_data$group <- gsub("|", "_links_", cell_data$group, fixed = TRUE)
table(cell_data$group)

genes <- rownames(multi.lin.sce)[seq_len(200)]
scmp_ob <- create_scmp(
    counts = counts(multi.lin.sce)[genes, ],
    cell_data = cell_data,
    ptime_col = "Monocle3_Pseudotime",
    path_col = "group"
)
```

# Each segment as a path

The first way treats the root, the link and the three end paths as five
paths. `sc.squeeze()` bins each of them along its own pseudotime, so the
bins of every segment start at 1:

```{r segments-bins, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Tile plot of the bins of the five segments, each binned from 1 along its
#|   own pseudotime.
seg_ob <- sc.squeeze(scmp_ob)
plotBinTile(seg_ob)
```

The model then compares each segment with a reference segment. With the
root as the reference, the terms of every other segment describe how it
differs from the root, at the same binned pseudotime. `reference` names it;
without it, `sc.set.poly()` takes the first path in C-locale (byte) order,
here `Y_15`, whose uppercase `Y` sorts before the lowercase `r` of `root`.

```{r segments-fit}
seg_ob <- sc.set.poly(seg_ob, poly_degree = 3, reference = "root")
seg_ob <- sc.p.vector(seg_ob, verbose = FALSE)
seg_ob <- sc.t.fit(seg_ob, verbose = FALSE)
seg_ob <- sc.filter(seg_ob, rsq = 0.6, vars = "groups")
seg_res <- scmpResults(seg_ob)
seg_lists <- as.data.frame(seg_res[, grep("^sig_", colnames(seg_res))])
colSums(seg_lists)
```

`sig_root` holds the genes that change along the root, and
`sig_Y_52vsroot`, for example, the genes whose profile in `Y_52` differs
from that in the root. The overlaps of the lists sort the genes by the
segments in which they differ from the root:

```{r segments-intersect, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   UpSet plot of the gene lists of the five segments with the root as the
#|   reference.
plotIntersect(seg_ob)
```

```{r segments-genes, include = FALSE}
link_like_root <- rownames(seg_lists)[
    seg_lists$sig_Y_15vsroot & seg_lists$sig_Y_18vsroot &
        seg_lists$sig_Y_52vsroot & !seg_lists$sig_Y_18_links_Y_15vsroot
]
```

For example, `r length(link_like_root)` genes differ from the root in all
three end paths but not in the link: along these genes the link carries on
the expression of the root, and the end paths leave it. One of them:

```{r segments-trend, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Trend of one gene in the five segments: the link follows the root, and the
#|   three end paths differ from it.
plotTrend(seg_ob, link_like_root[1], points = FALSE, lines = TRUE)
```

This view answers questions about the segments themselves, such as which
genes the link turns on, but every segment starts again at binned
pseudotime 1, so it does not follow a gene from the root to the end of a
lineage.

# The root and the link in every path

The second way follows each lineage from the start: the end path `Y_15`
holds the bins of the root, then those of the link, then its own, and so do
`Y_18` and `Y_52` with the segments on their way. `sc.restruct()` does this
after `sc.squeeze()`: it copies the bins of the root and of the links into
the end paths that share them, shifts the binned pseudotime of the later
bins to follow them, and computes the pseudo-bulk counts again.

```{r restruct, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Tile plot of the bins of the three end paths, each starting with the bins
#|   of the root.
lin_ob <- sc.restruct(sc.squeeze(scmp_ob),
    end_node_list = list("Y_15", "Y_18", "Y_52"),
    root_node = "root",
    link_node_list = list("Y_18_links_Y_15"),
    verbose = FALSE
)
plotBinTile(lin_ob)
```

The end paths now share their first bins, and the model compares whole
lineages. `sc.restruct()` puts the paths in the order of `end_node_list`, so
`Y_15` is the reference unless `reference` names another:

```{r restruct-fit}
lin_ob <- sc.set.poly(lin_ob, poly_degree = 3)
lin_ob <- sc.p.vector(lin_ob, verbose = FALSE)
lin_ob <- sc.t.fit(lin_ob, verbose = FALSE)
lin_ob <- sc.filter(lin_ob, rsq = 0.6, vars = "groups")
lin_res <- scmpResults(lin_ob)
colSums(as.data.frame(lin_res[, grep("^sig_", colnames(lin_res))]))
```

```{r restruct-clusters, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Trends of the clusters of the genes of the lists, one panel per cluster,
#|   with one curve per lineage.
lin_ob <- sc.cluster.trend(lin_ob, geneSet = "union", k = 4)
plotTrendCluster(lin_ob, verbose = FALSE)
```

## By hand

`sc.restruct()` handles a root, links and end paths. For other shapes,
build the bins by hand: take the bin table of `sc.squeeze()` with
`cDense()`, stack the bins of the segments of each lineage with their binned
pseudotime shifted, give the stacked bins the label of the lineage in the
path column, store the table with `cDense<-` and compute the pseudo-bulk
counts with `pb_counts()`. For this trajectory, the result is that of
`sc.restruct()`:

```{r by-hand}
bins <- cDense(sc.squeeze(scmp_ob))

stack_bins <- function(bins, segments, path) {
    out <- NULL
    shift <- 0
    for (segment in segments) {
        b <- bins[bins$group == segment, , drop = FALSE]
        b$scmp_binned_pseudotime <- b$scmp_binned_pseudotime + shift
        shift <- max(b$scmp_binned_pseudotime)
        out <- rbind(out, b)
    }
    out$group <- path
    rownames(out) <- paste(path, "bin", out$scmp_binned_pseudotime, sep = "_")
    out
}

hand_ob <- sc.squeeze(scmp_ob)
cDense(hand_ob) <- rbind(
    stack_bins(bins, c("root", "Y_18_links_Y_15", "Y_15"), "Y_15"),
    stack_bins(bins, c("root", "Y_18_links_Y_15", "Y_18"), "Y_18"),
    stack_bins(bins, c("root", "Y_52"), "Y_52")
)
hand_ob <- pb_counts(hand_ob)

restruct_ob <- sc.restruct(sc.squeeze(scmp_ob),
    end_node_list = list("Y_15", "Y_18", "Y_52"),
    root_node = "root",
    link_node_list = list("Y_18_links_Y_15"),
    verbose = FALSE
)
identical(eDense(hand_ob), eDense(restruct_ob))
```

# Choosing the reference path

The dummies of the model compare every path with the reference path, so the
reference decides what the coefficients and the `"groups"` lists of
`sc.filter()` say: with `Y_15` as the reference, `sig_Y_52vsY_15` lists the
genes whose profile in `Y_52` differs from that in `Y_15`. The full model is
the same with any reference, only written in other terms, so the p-values of
`sc.p.vector()` and its non-flat genes do not change, up to rounding. With
`Y_52`, the lineage that leaves the root on its own, as the reference:

```{r reference}
ref_ob <- sc.set.poly(lin_ob, poly_degree = 3, reference = "Y_52")
showPoly(ref_ob)
ref_ob <- sc.p.vector(ref_ob, verbose = FALSE)
all.equal(scmpResults(ref_ob)$p_value, lin_res$p_value)
identical(scmpResults(ref_ob)$non_flat, lin_res$non_flat)
ref_ob <- sc.t.fit(ref_ob, verbose = FALSE)
ref_ob <- sc.filter(ref_ob, rsq = 0.6, vars = "groups")
ref_res <- scmpResults(ref_ob)
colSums(as.data.frame(ref_res[, grep("^sig_", colnames(ref_res))]))
```

A good reference is the path the others are best described against: the
root when the segments are compared, a control or the most common fate
when lineages are compared. Without `reference`, the first path is the
first level of the path column when it is a factor, and otherwise the first
label in C-locale (byte) order, in every locale; after `sc.restruct()`, the
first path of `end_node_list`. Naming the reference keeps an analysis the
same when the labels change.
